title: Hybrid FlashAttention adapter and startup-warmup smoothing for v2/v3
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Integrating FlashAttention v2 and v3 into the serving runtime exposes startup and prefill latency regressions during warm kernels and mixed-variant routing. An abrupt switch to v3 kernels after a cold cache causes jitter and occasional token-latency spikes for short requests. Goal: Deliver an adaptive adapter that probes and blends v2/v3 kernels during startup and prefill, plus a light-weight smooth-warmup scheduler that reduces jitter without harming steady-state throughput. Success criteria: 1) Reduce 95th percentile token latency during first 5s of an active worker by >=30% for T5/LLM-like workloads compared to baseline, 2) No >5% throughput regression in steady state across our microbench fleet, 3) No new memory safety incidents in stress tests, and 4) Automated knob exposed in runtime config and Console toggle for experiment rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Perf test suite shows >=30% drop in startup 95p token latency on t5-like workloads (test harness: perf-harness/attn-startup v3)
End-to-end system tests show <5% throughput delta at 99th percentile under standard load profile
E2E canary (10% of traffic) runs for 48 hours with no memory-safety or OOM incidents
Feature flag + Console control implemented and documented (Console doc link in comments)
Design doc + bench notes reviewed by infra/rls and signoff from Reliability
technical_notes: Design: implement a small stateful adapter (kernel-adapter) that performs non-blocking micro-probes of alternate kernels on warmup paths. The adapter records micro-latency and memory pressure signals and computes an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) perf score per kernel-variant per model-shape.

Blending policy: choose a soft-transition schedule (0->1 blending) across first N prefill steps; default N=32, configurable by model profile. During blending we dispatch a fraction of batches to the alternate kernel to collect live stats rather than hard switchovers.

Probe instrumentation: cheap prefill probes use a reduced sequence length (prefill-sim=32) path to limit cost, and attach to existing kv-cache warmup hooks. Probes must be capped per-worker to avoid cross-traffic noise (default 1 probe / 10s per GPU).

Safety: when memory pressure or CUDA error is observed during a probe, adapter marks kernel-variant as degraded for cooldown period (default 60s) and falls back to safe-v2 layout. Add guarded try/catch and explicit stream synchronization only in probe path to avoid perturbing production decode paths.
Metrics: add kernel_adapter.probe.latency_ms, kernel_adapter.blend_ratio, kernel_adapter.degraded_flags, and runtime.prefill.jitter_ms. Wire these into Console and tracing for per-model slices.
Compatibility: ensure adapter works with quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) and with existing kernel selector. Adapter should expose hints to kernel-selector but not replace global heuristic scoring.
Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, start with internal canary (dev cluster), then 5% customer-facing nodes, then gradual ramp to 100% over two weeks with automated rollback on perf regression.

Testing: unit tests for EWMA scoring, simulated probe failures, integration tests on perf-harness with shuffled workload shapes, and fuzz tests for memory races in the probe path. Add a nightly job for prefill-warmup-regression detection.
Open questions: default blending window (N), probe frequency, and safe memory-pressure thresholds for heterogeneous instance types (A100 vs H100).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + prototype, 3d): implement kernel-adapter skeleton, basic EWMA scoring, and minimal probe loop. Add perf counters and local debug logging.
Phase 2 (integration, 4d): hook adapter into kernel-selector, implement blending policy, and add gating feature flag + Console toggle draft.
Phase 3 (hardening, 4d): add safety cooldowns, memory-pressure detection, quantized compatibility, and unit/integration tests.
Phase 4 (canary + measurement, 5d): deploy to internal canary, run perf-harness, collect metrics for 48 hours, iterate on thresholds.
Phase 5 (ramp + docs, 3d): open PR to enable 5% customer canary, publish Console docs and runbook, and schedule postmortem window after ramp completion.
risks_mitigation: Risk: probes perturb production latency. Mitigation: probe with tiny sequences on separate CUDA streams and cap frequency per worker.
Risk: EWMA mis-learns under bursty traffic. Mitigation: weighted windows + min-sample requirement before impacting routing decisions.
Risk: memory regressions on v3 kernels for some model shapes. Mitigation: automatic degraded flagging + immediate fallback to v2 and telemetry escalation.
Risk: interaction with existing autobalancer. Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler team; adapter will expose non-blocking hints only.
Risk: stealthy correctness regressions. Mitigation: preserve existing numerical outputs in blended path (compare sample outputs in test harness) and add regression alerting tied to eval prompt sets.
comments: 2026-03-09 Maya Patel: Created ticket. Attn: this was spawned from regression spike observed in incident INC-2026-03-03-ATTN where short-chat requests saw 2.1x 95p token latency during worker start.
2026-03-10 Luca Moretti: Initial prototype for adapter done locally. Observed 28% reduction in 95p startup latency on small microbench with H100 using blending N=16; need larger fleet tests.
2026-03-11 Reliability (review): Requested cooldown >=45s and a stricter min-sample of 8 probes before a switch. Also asked for explicit canary gating in autoscaler integration PR.

2026-03-12 QA: Added integration test matrix entries (shapes: 512x512, 1024x512, 2048x128) and quantized variants. Noted a reproducible OOM on 2048x128 with v3 when blending_ratio > 0.5 — investigation in progress.
